Senses.Explanation: To descend from the teaching seat. In the Chan record this is the standard visible close of a formal teaching-seat appearance: the person who mounted the seat may finish speaking, shout, strike or plant an implement, remain silent, or answer a demand by leaving. The action is not interchangeable with the preceding speech. Shakyamuni Buddha descends after Manjusri's sounding-block declaration in one Five Lamps scene and after his own refusal to preach in another. Tianyi Yihuai shouts and descends; Feiyin Tongrong descends only after the chief seat gives the closing declaration; and Langting Jingting says of passing geese, “They have passed,” before descending. Yaoshan Weiyan mounts the seat, remains silent, descends, and only afterward answers the rector in his quarters. When Zhaozhou Congshen asks Nanquan Puyuan to speak apart from the four propositions and hundred negations, Nanquan descends and returns to his quarters. The Linji Yixuan–Mayu Baoche exchange makes the actors especially important: Mayu first pulls Linji down and takes the seat, Linji then pulls Mayu down and retakes it, and Linji finally descends after Mayu leaves. Juelang Daosheng is preparing to descend when a lay questioner introduced as Huang Gong tells him, “Please step down.” These formal endings, commands, and forcible removals all preserve the same concrete movement away from the seat.

Senses.Note: Only one clear allowlisted occurrence of the contiguous upper-seat/lower-seat pair was found. The longer expression “lower-seat phrase” remains a nested lexical object and is not counted as another witness for this noun. Senses.Explanation: A rare nominal use for the lower of two seating positions, rather than the act of descending. In a Complete Collection of the Five Lamps encounter, Censor Wang first asks whether the bow is southern or northern and then whether it is from the upper or lower seat. Huayan Yu answers that neither end adheres and the middle is not secure either. The paired upper/lower alternatives make a seating-position referent explicit; the passage does not describe anyone leaving a seat.
